title: Export a photo for the web
summary: Save a light JPG copy for websites and email with Export As.

steps.say: Open a photo with Control O, or make sure one is already showing in the middle of the window.

check.prompt: Is a photo open and visible in the middle of the Photoshop window?

hints: Use File, then Open, and pick any JPG from your Pictures folder.
Dragging a photo file onto the Photoshop window opens it too.
steps.why: Every edit needs an open document to act on.

steps.say: Press Control Alt Shift W to open Export As.

checks.prompt: Is the Export As window open with a large preview of the image?

hints: It is under File, then Export, then Export As.
Click on the photo first so Photoshop has focus, then try the keys again.
steps.why: Export As makes a flat copy for sharing and keeps your original intact.

steps.say: On the right, under File Settings, set Format to JPG.

check.prompt: Is the Format set to JPG in the Export As window?

hints: Pick PNG instead if your image has see-through areas.
The Format menu is near the top of the right column.
steps.why: JPG is the usual choice for photos on websites.

steps.say: Set Quality to around 80 and watch the file size under the preview.

checks.prompt: Is the JPG quality setting around 80, between 60 and 90?

hints: Lower quality makes a smaller file but can add blocky patches.
Say done when the size looks reasonable.
steps.why: Quality trades file size against image detail.

steps.say: Under Image Size, type 1600 in the Width box if the photo is wider than that.

checks.prompt: Does the Image Size section show a width of 1600 or less?

hints: Skip this if the photo is already smaller.
Height updates by itself to keep the shape.
steps.why: Most web pages never show photos wider than this, so extra pixels only slow loading.

steps.say: Click Export at the bottom right, pick a folder, and click Save.

checks.prompt: Has the Export As window closed and the normal Photoshop workspace returned?

hints: If nothing happens, check whether a save window opened behind Photoshop.
Pictures is a good folder to find the file later.
steps.why: The exported file is ready to upload or attach to an email.
